definitions.explanation: a junior management position in Japanese companies, between supervisor and manager

examples.japanese: ⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{係長|かかりちょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なります→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I will become a section chief starting next month.

examples.japanese: {係長|かかりちょう}、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{書類|しょるい}→書類：01103_shorui⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{印鑑|いんかん}→印鑑：05290_inkan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧お{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Section chief, could you please stamp this document?

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{入社|にゅうしゃ}→入社：03131_nyuusha⟧⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧⟦{年目|ねんめ}→〜年目：28359_nenme⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{係長|かかりちょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{昇進|しょうしん}→昇進：04553_shoushin⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He was promoted to section chief in his fifth year at the company.

notes:
USAGE:
- {係長|かかりちょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{昇進|しょうしん}→昇進：04553_shoushin⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to be promoted to section chief)
- Can be used as a title when addressing someone
{係長|かかりちょう} is typically the first official management position in traditional Japanese companies. The title comes from ⟦{係|かかり}→係：02552_kakari⟧ (charge, duty) + {長|ちょう} (chief, head).

JAPANESE CORPORATE HIERARCHY:
⟦{平社員|ひらしゃいん}→平社員：16725_hirashain⟧ → ⟦{主任|しゅにん}→主任：08211_shunin⟧ → {係長|かかりちょう} → ⟦{課長|かちょう}→課長：01075_kachou⟧ → ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧
(Regular employee → Supervisor → Section chief → Manager → Department head)
